Source: skills/tmc-core-context/references/content-generation-playbook.md

# TMC Content Generation Playbook

Based on: the Content Generation workbook (Content Delivery and Content Distribution sections), adapted for TMC's B2B school audience and evidence rules. The workbook gives B2B, B2C and B2Ch tactics for each channel. **Only the B2B tactics are used.** The answered workbook exercises are in `content-strategy-workbook.md` and ready topics in `topic-bank.md`. The 4D strategy procedure is in `marketing-template-framework.md`. Brand visuals are in `brand-brief.md`.

Workbook statistics (platform user counts, ROI figures, survey percentages) are not adopted. They are generic and undated. Never quote them in TMC content without a current, cited source.

## Content delivery = design + skills

### Design elements
TMC's design decisions are already made in `brand-brief.md`. Apply the workbook's rules through it:

| Element | Workbook rule | TMC application |
|---|---|---|
| Colour | 2 to 3 colours chosen for brand emotion, used consistently | Paper White dominant, neutrals, Classroom Cyan accent (70 / 20 / 10) |
| Typography | One or two typefaces throughout | Staatliches for display, DM Sans for everything else |
| Image and video | Consistent editing style, logo placement, templates | Photo-overlay renderer style. Logo per brand brief. Approved trip photos only |
| Shapes and icons | Similar flat 2D icons across designs | One 1.5px-stroke line icon at most. No generic doodles |
| Logo | Meaningful, works in black and white | Primary and dark-mode logos. Never redrawn |
| Theme | Does this show what the brand stands for? | Educational partner, warm and specific. Would a parent understand it on a phone in five seconds? |

### Delivery skills (formats)
| Skill | Formats | TMC skill |
|---|---|---|
| Infographics | Single-image post, carousel, document post | `tmc-social-post`, `tmc-marketing-carousel` |
| Blogs | Listicle, detailed explanation, step-by-step guide | `tmc-blog` |
| Video | Informational, behind the scenes, interview, live Q&A, promo, testimonial or case study, lifestyle | `tmc-reel` (scripts only, production deferred) |
| Case studies and testimonials | Quote, unstructured (WhatsApp, comments), video, audio, reviews | `tmc-case-study` |
| Lead magnets | Checklist, guide, template, toolkit, webinar, assessment and more | `tmc-lead-magnet` |
| Email | Value add, quick win, free resource, case study, tip of the iceberg, promotional, engagement | `tmc-newsletter` |
| Social text posts | LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram caption, WhatsApp, X | `tmc-linkedin`, `tmc-social-post` |

## Infographics
Infographic = information + graphics. It is quick to read, shareable and relatively cheap to produce.

| Type | Content | TMC use |
|---|---|---|
| Educational | Tips, tricks, do's and don'ts, facts | Main type. Planning checklists, parent briefing tips, reflection prompts |
| Inspirational | Quotes | Only real, sourced quotes with permission. Never an invented testimonial |
| Promotional | Offers, ads, service information | Programme announcements only with approved details. No discounts without approval |
| Conversational | Polls, questions, fill in the blanks, caption this | LinkedIn and Instagram polls for principals, coordinators and teachers. No consumer giveaways or contests |
| Entertainment | Puzzles, comics, memes | Rare. Teacher audiences on Instagram only. Never for owners, trustees or management |

Rules: brand colours only, include the logo, embrace blank space, less is more, use images that support the message.

## Blogs
Blogs attract search traffic and leads, update readers, build credibility and trust, and build a following through consistent useful posts.

### Blog creation template
1. **Speak about the problem.** Hook the reader with the problem.
2. **Make the problem personal.** Show what readers usually feel about it.
3. **Discovery of the solution.** How the solution was found or the reframe.
4. **Solve the problem.** The practical answer.
5. **Call to action.** Point to the TMC resource or conversation that helps further.

### Blog types and title formulas
| Type | Title formula | TMC example |
|---|---|---|
| Listicle | Number of items + benefit or statement of fact | 7 Questions to Ask Before Approving a School Trip |
| Detailed explanation | What is / What are + context | What Is Experiential Learning? A Guide for School Leaders |
| Step-by-step guide | How to + benefit + number of steps | How to Plan a Curriculum-Linked Domestic Tour in 6 Steps |

Counts in titles must match the content delivered.

## Video (scripts)
Video production is deferred. Scripts can be drafted as text assets with the templates below.

Hook timing: 3 seconds on YouTube, Facebook, LinkedIn and WhatsApp. 1 second on Instagram and YouTube Shorts.

### Informational video
1. Opening: grab attention (3 s, or 1 s on Reels and Shorts).
2. Introduction: who is speaking. Skip on Reels.
3. Seeding (about 6 s): one verified instance that earns the right to speak on the topic. Skip on Reels.
4. Value: educate, entertain or inspire, as bullet points or a story.
5. CTA: continue the conversation (comment, share, DM, answer a question).
6. Sign-off.

### Interview video
Edification (build-up about the guest) → introduction → education or inspiration → CTA → sign-off. Guests: educators, principals, subject experts. Needs the guest's consent to publish.

### Promotion video (programme or webinar)
Press the pain point → programme intro and takeaways → speaker intro → invitation and CTA → sign-off. Programme details must be approved.

### Testimonial or case study video
Hook (problem or verified result) → situation → complication → question → answer (TMC's intervention and before and after) → CTA. Evidence and consent rules from `tmc-case-study` apply.

### YouTube long-form script (8 to 12 minutes)
| Part | Length | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | 3 s | A quote, statement or number (sourced) |
| Why me | 3 s | Earn the right to speak on the topic |
| Why should you care | 30 s | The cost of ignoring the problem |
| Watch-to-the-end anchor | 5 s | Seed the lead magnet CTA |
| Expand the problem | 2 min | What the problem leads to |
| Solution | 5 min | The main content |
| New reality | 2 min | What changes when the reader applies it |
| CTA | end | The right lead magnet with its link |

### Video production tips (for briefs)
Thumbnail with title and image, brand guidelines applied, plain or appealing background, look at the camera, camera at eye level, talk to the viewer rather than present, smile, tripod, light facing the speaker, a microphone, subtitles.

## Case studies and testimonials
Case studies give social proof by showing a customer's before and after, written by TMC. Testimonials are recommendations from satisfied customers in their own words. Both establish relatability, show impact, build credibility and increase conversions.

### Case study framework (SCAI)
1. **Situation:** who the school is (with permission to name, or anonymised).
2. **Complication:** the specific problem the school faced.
3. **Answer:** what TMC designed or did.
4. **Impact:** the verified outcome.

Draft template and evidence list: `tmc-case-study`.

### Testimonial types
Quote (one to three sentences), unstructured (WhatsApp messages, comments on posts), video, audio, consumer reviews (Google, social media). Each needs the author's permission for marketing use and a stored source.

### Questions that produce useful testimonials
Ask schools, teachers and parents after a programme:
1. What problem did the programme solve for you or your students?
2. What made you choose TMC?
3. Which parts of the programme worked best?
4. What made you happiest about the experience?
5. What would be the main reason you would recommend TMC to another school?

Record the answer verbatim with date, name, role and permission scope. Never edit a quote's meaning.

## Lead magnets
A lead magnet is something useful offered in exchange for contact details.

| Type | Examples | TMC fit |
|---|---|---|
| Educational | Course, webinar, tutorial | Webinar for principals on planning curriculum-linked trips |
| Solution-based | Checklist, toolkit, template | School Trip Assurance Checklist (agreed foundation asset), proposal comparison template, parent briefing pack |
| Community | WhatsApp group, Facebook group | Teacher community for trip leaders. Needs moderation and consent rules |
| Entertaining | E-book, quiz, assessment, challenge | Readiness assessment: is your school ready for an international programme? |
| Promotional | Free trial, free consultation, free design | Free programme design consultation. Needs approval before offering |

Other formats: templates, scripts, ultimate guides, tutorials, event tickets, free chapters, coupons. Coupons and discounts need commercial approval.

## Email
### High-impact email in six steps
1. Clear goal: what this email should achieve and which content achieves it.
2. Subject line: the most important part of the content, with an action word.
3. Layout: placement of copy, images and links.
4. Introduction: a few sentences that hook the reader and say what the email is about.
5. Core content: the value. Visuals such as a chart or table where useful.
6. Conclusion and CTA: short summary, links to further resources, one action.

### Email types
| Type | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Value add | Address a need or emotion and show expertise |
| Quick win | Help the reader get a small result fast |
| Free resource | Give away a useful tool or resource |
| Case study | Share a verified school story and what made it work |
| Tip of the iceberg | Share part of the content and link to the rest |
| Promotional | Persuade the reader to act now. Only approved offers |
| Engagement | Surveys, feedback requests, thank-you notes |

B2B email practice (the only practice used): segment by role, school and interaction; nurture with automated sequences; share guides and case studies; test subject lines and CTAs; follow up on engagement that did not convert. Never use false urgency.

## Distribution: channel playbooks
Paid advertising setup is out of scope for this release. These playbooks cover organic content. TMC is B2B: every channel's job is to reach a school role or help one decide. B2C tactics (shops, shopping tags, consumer discounts, user contests, cart recovery, flash sales) and B2Ch tactics (partner catalogues, channel incentives) are not used. Channel roles and tactics in one table: `content-strategy-workbook.md`, section 6.

### LinkedIn (primary B2B channel)
- Accounts: TMC company page and Yasin's personal profile. See `tmc-linkedin`.
- Content: insights, frameworks, document carousels, short videos, case studies, polls.
- Engage in education leadership groups and discussions with useful comments, not promotion.
- Webinars for principals can be promoted here.
- Track: posts, followers or connections, new connections, reach, search appearances.

### Instagram
- Role: proof and culture for school audiences. Show programme culture, preparation and real trip moments. Visual storytelling humanises TMC for principals, coordinators and teachers. Parents of client schools may see TOUR posts, but they are not the target.
- Carousels explain processes. Story highlights hold case studies, testimonials and FAQs.
- Use a small set of relevant education hashtags. Reply personally to DMs from school staff and offer a planning conversation.
- Track: posts, followers, new followers, profile visit to follow conversion, engagement rate, saves and shares.

### Facebook
- Business page with complete About, contact and website details.
- Share guides, case studies and trip documentation that school leaders can use and forward.
- Participate in educator and principal groups without overt promotion. Parent groups are not a lead source.
- Track: posts, followers, new followers, reach, engagement rate, video views.

### YouTube (deferred with video)
- Webinars, explainers, interviews with educators, trip films.
- Optimise titles, descriptions and tags. Put the lead magnet link high in the description. Pin a CTA comment. Use playlists by topic.
- Track: videos posted, average view duration, views, subscribers, new subscribers.

### WhatsApp
- Use WhatsApp Business (or the Business API at scale) with greeting, away and quick-reply messages, labels and a programme catalogue.
- Broadcast lists for school contacts who opted in. Personalised follow-ups after meetings. Status for updates.
- Never broadcast marketing to parents.
- Consent first. Parent groups during trips are operational channels, not marketing lists.
- Share square (1080 × 1080) images.

### SMS
- Reminders only: meeting confirmations, webinar reminders, post-meeting follow-ups to school contacts who agreed to receive them.
- Send in business hours. One clear action. No promotions or flash offers.

### Email
See Email above and `tmc-newsletter`. Track: database size, emails sent, open rate, click-through rate, bounce rate. Opens alone are not proof of interest.

### SEO and blog
- Keyword research from `audience-personas.md` keywords and real search data.
- On-page: keyword in title, headings, meta description and body, used naturally. Internal links between related posts.
- Off-page: quality backlinks from education sites and partner schools.
- Track: blog count, blog views, time on page, website sessions, new and returning users, exit rates on home, programmes and enquiry pages.

### Google Business Profile
- Complete profile, photos, posts and updates. Encourage genuine reviews from schools and parents and respond to each one.
- Never write or solicit fake reviews.

### X (Twitter)
- Not a lead-generation channel. Consider only after LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook and email work consistently.
- If used: real-time education conversations, one or two relevant hashtags, promote blog posts.

### Offline distribution
School workshops and presentations, education expos and fairs, brochures and flyers, and personal meetings with decision-makers. Content assets (checklists, case studies, guides) should be printable for these.

## Choosing a platform
1. **Audience presence:** is the decision-maker there? Owners, trustees and principals: LinkedIn, email, WhatsApp, in person. Management: email, WhatsApp. Coordinators and teachers: LinkedIn, Instagram, WhatsApp.
2. **Engagement:** where does that audience actually engage?
3. **Ease of execution:** start with the channels the team can sustain.

## Role of the business owner
Yasin leads content strategy and founder content, sets up systems to track data, reviews the strategy, and reviews the team's and agencies' performance. Ad operations, design production, copywriting and platform technicalities can be delegated.


---

Source: skills/tmc-core-context/references/content-taxonomy.md

# TMC Content Taxonomy

Every asset carries these fields where practical. MARKETING assets need all fields marked required. TOUR assets need the fields marked T.

| Field | Values | Required |
|---|---|---|
| content_id | `TMC-YYYYMMDD-<FORMAT>-NNN`. Formats: LI, FB, IG, CAR, BLOG, NEWS, CASE, LM (lead magnet), WA (WhatsApp), WEB, VID (script) | yes, T |
| master_idea_id | Shared ID across repurposed versions of one idea | if repurposed |
| content_category | TOUR, MARKETING | yes, T |
| target_audience | owner_trustee, management, principal, academic_coordinator, teacher (B2B: always a school role; parents and students are voices, recorded in `voice_source`) | yes, T |
| voice_source | Parent, student, teacher or educator whose words or work appear, with consent reference, or "none" | if voices used |
| school_segment | A, B, C (`audience-personas.md`) or unknown | if targeted |
| content_bucket | 1 to 7 (`content-buckets.md`). One primary only | yes, T |
| customer_emotion | fear, pain_point, problem, need, desire, fantasy + the specific item | yes |
| content_angle | One of the 33 angles (`marketing-template-framework.md`) | yes |
| funnel_stage | awareness, consideration, proof, conversion, nurture | yes |
| programme | day_trip, domestic_tour, international_tour, general | if relevant |
| objective | What this asset should cause | yes |
| topic | Working title | yes, T |
| hook | First line | yes |
| core_message | One sentence | yes |
| proof_required | Claim IDs from the claims register, or "none" | yes, T |
| claim_risk | low, medium, high | yes |
| delivery_type | infographic, carousel, text_post, blog, email, case_study, lead_magnet, video_script, photo_dump | yes, T |
| platform | linkedin_yasin, linkedin_company, instagram, facebook, email, blog, website, whatsapp, youtube, x | yes, T |
| account_voice | yasin, company | for LinkedIn |
| photo_requirement | Brief or "none" | yes, T |
| media_permission | APPROVED, DENIED, UNKNOWN, NOT_APPLICABLE per category | if media, T |
| CTA | One action and its verified destination, or "none" | yes |
| source_materials | Files, notes, URLs | yes, T |
| approval_status | Workflow state | yes, T |

## Funnel stages
- **Awareness:** insight, problem recognition, founder perspective. Usual buckets: 1, 6.
- **Consideration:** frameworks, safety and governance, buyer guides, parent confidence, curriculum fit. Usual buckets: 2, 3, 4, 7.
- **Proof:** case studies, testimonials, evidenced outcomes, process evidence. Usual bucket: 5.
- **Conversion:** planner, consultation, resource, conversation. Usual bucket: 7.
- **Nurture:** newsletters, follow-up content, deeper proof.

## Idea quality gate
Reject or rewrite an idea if any answer is yes:
1. Could any generic school-tour company publish this unchanged?
2. Is it only destination inspiration?
3. Does it lack a clear decision-maker (or, for TOUR, a real trip moment)?
4. Does it depend on an unsupported claim?
5. Is it purely promotional?
6. Does it speak to more than one primary audience?
7. Does it fit no bucket, or need two buckets to make sense?
8. Is it written to sell to parents or students (B2C) rather than to help a school role decide?
9. Does its CTA ask a family, rather than a school, to act?

If question 1 is yes, rewrite until the piece contains a distinct TMC point of view, verified proof, or school-specific usefulness.

# TMC Measurement, Cadence and Calendar

Based on: Understanding The Modern Classroom guide (posting schedule, metrics, KPIs), the Content Generation workbook (measurement metrics, marketing calendar sample), and `system/WORKFLOW.md` (contracted non-video capacity).

## Posting cadence
Two numbers exist. Use the contracted capacity for production planning unless the team records a change.

| Platform | Contracted non-video capacity per month (WORKFLOW) | Ideal schedule per month (Understanding TMC guide) |
|---|---|---|
| LinkedIn | 12 (8 Yasin personal, 4 company) | 12 |
| Instagram | 4 | 20, including 8 reels |
| Facebook | 4 | 8 |
| Email | 2 | 4 newsletters + 2 lead magnets |
| Blog | 2 | 6 |
| Website asset | 1 | not set |
| YouTube | deferred (video) | 4 long videos + 8 shorts |
| X (Twitter) | not in scope | 16 |
| **Total** | **25** | **74 + video** |

The guide's digital plan also says "at least 3 to 5 social posts a week". The ideal schedule is a growth target. Reaching it needs more production capacity, video and an X decision. Monthly reviews should report progress against the contracted number first.

## Marketing calendar format
One row per placement. The first eight columns are the workbook's calendar. The rest link it to TMC's job records and tracker.

| Column | Values |
|---|---|
| Posting date | YYYY-MM-DD |
| Platform | LinkedIn (Yasin), LinkedIn (company), Instagram, Facebook, Email, Blog, Website, WhatsApp, YouTube, X |
| Content bucket | 1 to 7 (`content-buckets.md`) |
| Needs and emotions | Fear, Pain point, Problem, Need, Desire, Fantasy + the specific item |
| Content strategy (delivery type) | Infographic, carousel, text post, blog, video script, email, case study, lead magnet |
| Content topic | Working title |
| Status | INTAKE, DRAFT, NEEDS_INPUT, REVIEW, CHANGES_REQUESTED, APPROVED, RENDERING_PENDING, EXPORTED, PUBLISHED |
| Caption | Draft caption or first line |
| Content ID | `TMC-YYYYMMDD-<FORMAT>-NNN` |
| Audience | From `audience-personas.md` |
| Angle | One of the 33 angles |
| Funnel stage | awareness, consideration, proof, conversion, nurture |
| Category | TOUR or MARKETING |
| Proof needed | Claim IDs or "none" |
| Version and file link | Latest version and its file |
| Live URL | After publication only |

Example row: `2026-11-12 | LinkedIn (company) | 7 | Problem: comparing two proposals | Text post | Five questions to ask before signing a tour proposal | DRAFT | "Two proposals, same destination, very different trips." | TMC-20261112-LI-001 | Principal | Questions to ask before | consideration | MARKETING | none | v001 jobs/... | -`

A shared sample calendar exists as a Google Sheet linked from the Understanding TMC guide. This workspace has no connection to it. Provide copyable rows when it is not connected.

## Metrics by platform
Collect these monthly. Missing data is unknown, not zero. State the reporting window.

| Platform | Metrics |
|---|---|
| Instagram | Total posts, new posts in period, followers, new followers, profile visit to follow conversion, engagement rate (Ninjalytics is the stated tool), saves and shares, followers gained from live sessions |
| Facebook | Posts in period, followers, new followers, post reach, engagement rate, video views |
| LinkedIn | Posts, total connections or followers, new connections, reach, search appearances |
| YouTube | Videos posted, average view duration, total views, total subscribers, new subscribers |
| Email | Database size, emails sent, open rate, click-through rate, bounce rate |
| Website | Session duration, new users, returning users, exit rate on home, programmes and enquiry pages |
| Lead magnets | New contacts generated |
| Blog | Number of blogs, total views, time spent |

## Business KPIs
These decide success. Reach metrics only explain them.

1. **Leads generated:** enquiries and bookings received.
2. **Qualified school conversations:** conversations with decision-makers at target-segment schools.
3. **Conversion rate:** share of leads that become customers.
4. **Website traffic and behaviour.**
5. **Social engagement:** likes, comments, shares, follower growth.
6. **Customer feedback:** collected and analysed from schools, parents and students.

Where possible, tag each lead with the content ID that started it.

## Monthly review decisions
For each bucket, platform and format, recommend Continue, Improve, Test, Reduce or Stop, with the evidence. Keep the reasoning for next month's calendar.

# TMC Claims Register Template

Maintain the live register outside the generation prompt as the authority for factual claims. This template is not an approved register. The seeded rows below record claims found in TMC's own planning documents. None is approved for publication.

| Claim ID | Claim | Status | Source | Approved wording | Restrictions | Last verified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CLM-001 | TMC is based in Bangalore | VERIFY | Understanding TMC guide | | Low risk. Confirm current address before use in contact details | |
| CLM-002 | TMC runs day trips, domestic educational tours and international educational tours | VERIFY | Understanding TMC guide | | Low risk. Confirm current programme list | |
| CLM-003 | TMC has comprehensive safety protocols, experienced tour directors and detailed planning | VERIFY | Understanding TMC guide (USP) | | Describe specific confirmed processes instead of the general claim. No "top priority" or guarantee language | |
| CLM-004 | Programmes are customised to each school's educational needs and goals | VERIFY | Understanding TMC guide (USP) | | Needs a confirmed example of customisation | |
| CLM-005 | Numerous testimonials from schools, parents and students show the value of TMC programmes | VERIFY | Understanding TMC guide (USP) | | Use individual sourced testimonials with permission. Never a count without records | |
| CLM-006 | TMC has successfully conducted a wide range of tours | VERIFY | Understanding TMC guide (USP) | | Any number of tours, schools or students needs records | |
| CLM-007 | Programmes develop leadership, teamwork, cultural awareness and confidence | VERIFY | Understanding TMC guide (USP) | | Say "designed to develop". Claim achieved outcomes only with bucket 5 evidence | |
| CLM-008 | Planning targets: 100 schools, 2,00,000 children, annual student targets by programme | PROHIBITED | Understanding TMC guide | | Internal planning only. Never publish | |
| CLM-009 | School segment labels and the product funnel classification | PROHIBITED | Understanding TMC guide | | Internal planning only. Never publish | |

## Status
- APPROVED: may be used exactly or conservatively paraphrased.
- VERIFY: do not publish until checked.
- RESTRICTED: only use in specified contexts.
- PROHIBITED: do not use in published content.

## High-risk claim classes
Always verify:
- years in operation
- number of schools, students or trips
- safety records
- medical or emergency performance
- prices and packages
- visa and travel rules
- curriculum or board alignment
- measurable student outcomes
- school or client names
- testimonials and reviews
- parent feedback
- facilitator qualifications
- performance percentages
- external statistics (need a current, cited source)
